001package com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.response.historyLog;
002
003import java.util.Arrays;
004
005import org.apache.commons.lang3.Validate;
006import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.annotations.HistoryLogProps;
007import com.jwoglom.pumpx2.pump.messages.helpers.Bytes;
008
009/**
010 * Once-a-day Tandem Mobi summary of the BLE connections made to the pump. The pump writes it every
011 * 24 hours counted from its last restart, not at midnight, so its time of day differs between pumps
012 * and each record covers the 24 hours since the previous one. The header timestamp is the end of
013 * that period.
014 *
015 * <p>The counts were compared with the connections and JPAKE authentications TandemKit logged in
016 * 12 day-long windows on two pumps (the maintainer's and a tester's).
017 * {@link #getConnections()} minus {@link #getUnauthenticatedConnections()} equalled the number of
018 * authenticated sessions in all 12 windows. The class name is provisional: opcode 474 is not in
019 * Tandem's cloud event schema or the Mobi app's history log list. Fields not named here have not
020 * been identified and are exposed raw. See https://github.com/jwoglom/pumpx2/issues/152.
021 */
022@HistoryLogProps(
023    opCode = 474,
024    displayName = "BLE Daily Connections"
025)
026public class BleDailyConnectionsHistoryLog extends HistoryLog {
027
028    private int connectedPercent;
029    private int unknown11;
030    private int connections;
031    private int unauthenticatedConnections;
032    private byte[] unknownTail;
033
034    public BleDailyConnectionsHistoryLog() {}
035    public BleDailyConnectionsHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int connectedPercent, int unknown11, int connections, int unauthenticatedConnections, byte[] unknownTail) {
036        super(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum);
037        this.cargo = buildCargo(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, connectedPercent, unknown11, connections, unauthenticatedConnections, unknownTail);
038        this.connectedPercent = connectedPercent;
039        this.unknown11 = unknown11;
040        this.connections = connections;
041        this.unauthenticatedConnections = unauthenticatedConnections;
042        this.unknownTail = Arrays.copyOfRange(this.cargo, 16, 26);
043    }
044
045    public BleDailyConnectionsHistoryLog(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int connectedPercent, int unknown11, int connections, int unauthenticatedConnections) {
046        this(pumpTimeSec, sequenceNum, connectedPercent, unknown11, connections, unauthenticatedConnections, new byte[10]);
047    }
048
049    public int typeId() {
050        return 474;
051    }
052
053    /**
054     * <table border="1">
055     * <caption>Parsed fields for BleDailyConnectionsHistoryLog:</caption>
056     * <tr><td><code>connectedPercent</code></td><td><code>raw[10] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
057     * <tr><td><code>unknown11</code></td><td><code>raw[11] &amp; 0xFF</code></td></tr>
058     * <tr><td><code>connections</code></td><td><code>Bytes.readShort(raw, 12)</code></td></tr>
059     * <tr><td><code>unauthenticatedConnections</code></td><td><code>Bytes.readShort(raw, 14)</code></td></tr>
060     * <tr><td><code>unknownTail</code></td><td><code>Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, 16, 26)</code></td></tr>
061     * </table>
062     */
063    public void parse(byte[] raw) {
064        Validate.isTrue(raw.length == 26);
065        this.cargo = raw;
066        parseBase(raw);
067        this.connectedPercent = raw[10] & 0xFF;
068        this.unknown11 = raw[11] & 0xFF;
069        this.connections = Bytes.readShort(raw, 12);
070        this.unauthenticatedConnections = Bytes.readShort(raw, 14);
071        this.unknownTail = Arrays.copyOfRange(raw, 16, 26);
072    }
073
074    public static byte[] buildCargo(long pumpTimeSec, long sequenceNum, int connectedPercent, int unknown11, int connections, int unauthenticatedConnections, byte[] unknownTail) {
075        Validate.isTrue(unknownTail.length == 10, "unknownTail must be 10 bytes");
076        return HistoryLog.fillCargo(Bytes.combine(
077            HistoryLog.typeIdBytes(474, 0),
078            Bytes.toUint32(pumpTimeSec),
079            Bytes.toUint32(sequenceNum),
080            Bytes.firstByteLittleEndian(connectedPercent),
081            Bytes.firstByteLittleEndian(unknown11),
082            Bytes.firstTwoBytesLittleEndian(connections),
083            Bytes.firstTwoBytesLittleEndian(unauthenticatedConnections),
084            unknownTail));
085    }
086
087    /**
088     * The share of the 24 hours during which the pump had a BLE connection, apparently rounded to
089     * the nearest percent. Values of 97-100 were observed. It matched the phone-side connected time
090     * in 11 of 12 windows; the twelfth was 0.02 points below the rounding threshold. It read 100
091     * with {@link #getConnections()} 0 on a day with no reconnection.
092     * Medium confidence.
093     *
094     * @return percent of the period with a BLE connection, 0-100
095     */
096    public int getConnectedPercent() {
097        return connectedPercent;
098    }
099
100    /**
101     * Constant per pump: 6 on both of the maintainer's Mobis, 4 on a tester's. Its meaning is
102     * unknown, and it is not a firmware or model code.
103     *
104     * @return raw uint8 at offset 11
105     */
106    public int getUnknown11() {
107        return unknown11;
108    }
109
110    /**
111     * BLE connections the pump accepted during the period, including ones that failed encryption
112     * or never authenticated. Values of 0-66 were observed. This equalled the connections the phone
113     * logged (connects plus encryption failures) in 8 of 12 windows. In the other 4 it was exactly
114     * 2 higher, from connections the phone never reported. Byte 13 was 0 in every record, so it is
115     * read as a uint16; byte 12 alone gives the same values.
116     *
117     * @return number of BLE connections in the period
118     */
119    public int getConnections() {
120        return connections;
121    }
122
123    /**
124     * Connections during the period that never completed JPAKE authentication (key confirmation),
125     * including failed encryption and links dropped during setup. Values of 0-11 were observed. The
126     * value was 0 exactly on the days the phone logged no failed, cancelled or timed-out
127     * connection. Byte 15 was always 0, so it is read as a uint16, like {@link #getConnections()}.
128     *
129     * @return number of connections that did not authenticate
130     */
131    public int getUnauthenticatedConnections() {
132        return unauthenticatedConnections;
133    }
134
135    /**
136     * Equal to the authenticated sessions TandemKit logged in 12 of 12 windows on two pumps.
137     *
138     * @return {@link #getConnections()} minus {@link #getUnauthenticatedConnections()}
139     */
140    public int getAuthenticatedConnections() {
141        return connections - unauthenticatedConnections;
142    }
143
144    /**
145     * Bytes 16-25. Zero in every record examined. No new pairing happened in any window
146     * examined, so a pairing counter here would also have read 0.
147     *
148     * @return a copy of bytes 16-25
149     */
150    public byte[] getUnknownTail() {
151        return Arrays.copyOf(unknownTail, unknownTail.length);
152    }
153}
